island seed
Big recent moves resolve in the direction of the established six-month trend because trend followers add on volatility.
Volatility-normalised MACD spread: trend followers act on this crossing, so the level proxies for continued mechanical demand.
Fraction of up days measures how steadily information arrives; steady drift is under-extrapolated relative to jumpy moves.
Momentum earned with low volatility comes from steady fundamental news rather than speculative churn, so it persists longer.
Established trend combined with a one-day setback buys the trend at a liquidity discount rather than at the top tick.
Risk-adjusted six-month drift favours trends produced by many small informed trades rather than one repricing event.
Reversal pay-off scales with volatility because the inventory risk premium market makers charge is larger in volatile names.
A single outsized up day within the week marks attention-driven buying by retail traders, which is systematically reversed.
Normalising the monthly deviation by typical daily range measures overextension in units of how far the stock usually travels in a day.
High-volatility names have wider effective spreads, so the compensation for supplying liquidity against three-day moves is larger there.
Only days exceeding the stock's own volatility are large enough to be pressure, so reversal is applied selectively and momentum otherwise.
Days spent above the widely watched fifty-day average count how persistently trend followers have been long, proxying continued support.
A six-month high set recently but a monthly high set some days ago means the stock is consolidating gains rather than topping.
Momentum that survives into a calm period has been accepted by the market, whereas momentum with rising volatility is being contested.
A shallow worst day over the quarter indicates absence of crash risk and of forced deleveraging in the shareholder base.
Volatility high relative to mean absolute move indicates fat-tailed jump risk, and jump-prone names carry a negative return premium.
Net up-day count over a month measures breadth of buying interest rather than the size of any single repricing event.
Persistent directional breadth plus a short pullback is the cleanest entry into a diffusing information trend.
Dispersion of weekly returns measures path roughness, and rough paths deter the patient capital that sustains drift.
Repeatedly resetting the quarterly low identifies persistent distribution, where an unfinished seller keeps supplying stock.
Price rising with volume over short windows marks attention-driven chasing, which exhausts once the crowd is fully positioned.
A strengthening price-volume link over a month indicates new participants arriving, which sustains the move rather than ending it.
Volume confirming the direction of the quarterly trend distinguishes accumulation from distribution when the correlation sign is ambiguous.
Trends supported by steady turnover come from ongoing reallocation, whereas trends on spiky turnover come from event traders who leave.
Opening gaps overshoot because they clear at a single auction price with thin depth, and the excess is corrected intraday.
Strong closes coinciding with heavy volume identify genuine accumulation rather than a thin drift up on no participation.
Frequency of positive intraday sessions over a quarter captures persistent daytime demand independent of overnight gaps.
Successively higher monthly peaks over a quarter mark a sequence of cleared resistance levels that anchoring investors under-react to.
Repeated intraday excursions above the open that are not held show buyers being met with supply, which caps subsequent moves.
A high earnings yield gives fundamental support that makes a two-week sell-off far more likely to be temporary pressure.
Improving returns on equity while the price falls is a divergence that resolves toward the fundamentals once selling pressure ends.
daily Amihud impact: a name whose price moves far per dollar traded pays an illiquidity premium
square-root impact law: execution cost scales with the root of size, so root depth is the right normaliser
Kyle lambda proxy: volatility per unit of log market depth is what a market maker must be paid for
intraday range bought with each dollar of volume is a direct measure of how thin the book is
own-history percentile of share impact isolates episodic liquidity droughts from permanent size
close-to-close move as a multiple of the normal intraday range: repricing the auction cannot absorb
today's value traded as a fraction of the quarter's busiest day scales attention without a size bias
volume surprise against the stock's own month: trading interest arriving ahead of the price move
month-on-month change in participation, normalised by level: rising interest is faded once crowded
count of above-baseline sessions measures breadth of participation rather than one outsized day
time since the quietest session; a recent trading vacuum precedes wider spreads and higher required return
fading interest: participation below its own long-run level means the marginal buyer has left
two-month against nine-month participation, the horizon over which institutional accumulation shows
half-year accumulation imbalance: slow institutional building that continues after it is measured
does participation rise with weekly gains: sustained demand elasticity predicts continued inflow
big moves arriving with rising volume are informed; the same moves on falling volume are noise
root participation makes the volatility-volume link robust to block prints over a long window
dollar depth arriving with big moves is liquidity supply meeting demand; its absence is fragility
a rising price-to-flow elasticity means liquidity supply is withdrawing, which is repriced with a lag
root dollar depth against absolute moves matches the square-root impact law execution desks use
a two-week price-volume lockstep marks a crowded short-term trade whose flow is about to stop
rank coupling of depth and movement, immune to the level differences that dominate raw correlations
monthly range-volume coupling separates orderly two-sided markets from one-sided liquidity events
today's range against its own quarterly norm is a clean intraday liquidity shock
intraday range relative to close-to-close variation isolates microstructure noise from real repricing
log range is a scale-free Parkinson-style cost estimate that does not depend on the price level
upper versus lower shadow: persistent selling into strength means supply overhangs the book
intraday travel that produced no net move is two-sided churn that liquidity providers are paid for
Parkinson against close-to-close volatility; the wedge is bid-ask bounce, a direct spread proxy
days since the widest session: the inventory imbalance created that day decays with time
quarter-on-quarter change in relative range is a slow change in the cost of trading the name
monthly intraday travel per unit of realised move measures round-trip churn absorbed by dealers
weekly range acceleration relative to baseline flags liquidity withdrawing before prices react
count of wide sessions in the last month measures persistence of a costly-to-trade regime
the calmest day of the month sets the floor on trading cost, where the liquidity premium disappears
where the open sits in the range measures the overnight order imbalance the auction had to clear
heavy volume with a weak close is supply hitting bids, and that inventory has to be re-sold
buying pressure arriving with volume confirms real demand rather than a thin-book drift
how far price falls below the open before support appears measures resting bid depth
coefficient of variation of participation: unpredictable liquidity forces investors to demand a premium
log volume dispersion over half a year measures structural, not event-driven, liquidity uncertainty
stable dollar depth lets arbitrageurs size positions, so mispricings there are corrected faster
recency-weighted participation against a stale baseline captures acceleration a plain ratio misses
day-to-day volume churn measures how unreliable tomorrow's liquidity is for sizing a trade
half-year participation instability is a slow-moving liquidity-risk state that earns a premium
how recently the month's biggest dollar day happened; fresh price pressure has not yet decayed
average short-run volume noise against long-run dispersion separates chronic lumpiness from an episode
volatility of the daily volume innovation: names whose participation jumps around are slow to arbitrage
share participation high while dollar participation is not means small tickets, a retail-attention footprint
high-volume moves are liquidity demand and reverse; low-volume moves are information and continue
a month's trend is only tradable while depth is available to support it
a trend not yet accompanied by rising participation is under-owned and has further to run
a few days of gains in a name with a solid liquidity floor is real demand, not a thin-book artifact
the best day of the fortnight, made on abnormal dollar flow, is the part of the move that reverses
when monthly trend and participation move together the flow is trend-following and eventually exhausts
the accrual anomaly survives where unstable liquidity keeps arbitrage capital away
earnings yield is compensated more where price impact makes the position costly to hold
an improvement in profitability only enters the price on days when someone is actually trading it
return on equity is slow to be priced in stocks whose intraday cost of trading is high
profitable names that have gone quiet since their volume peak are neglected quality
return on book is impounded fastest in the week attention arrives
cheap earnings in a stock quiet since its liquidity trough is a neglect trade
efficient operators in names with inelastic liquidity supply carry both a quality and an illiquidity claim
profitability is repriced during clusters of busy sessions, not on a single print
book value against the day's ceiling price, rewarded where liquidity is too erratic to arbitrage
attention regimes reward profitability, quiet regimes reward cheapness
the profitability premium is largest in the half of the panel where price impact is worst
unlevered profitability is rewarded when the stock trades at the top of its own volume history
sales generated per unit of assets, penalised for the balance-sheet risk taken to get there
accruals scaled by book are the part of reported earnings least likely to convert into cash
pricing power that shows up in cash rather than in accrual estimates is the durable half of margin
improving profitability that is cash-backed rather than accrual-driven is the durable half of the signal
return on equity net of the leverage that manufactured it isolates genuine operating quality
Book-to-price measured at the open, which is the price a T+1 entry actually pays; assets bought below replacement value mean-revert.
EPS over VWAP prices value at the level investors actually transacted, not at a possibly unrepresentative closing print.
Book is worth more per dollar of price when the assets behind it earn a margin; margin-weighting screens out value traps.
Earnings yield weighted by asset profitability keeps cheap-and-good names and drops cheap-because-broken ones.
Sales-generating assets per dollar of price is a sales-yield proxy that avoids margin-accounting distortion.
Price per unit of absolute earnings: the most expensive names on any earnings base carry the highest expectation risk.
Earnings yield tilted toward firms that also turn assets quickly, where earnings are volume-driven rather than one-off.
Leverage amplifies flow-driven price moves, so the mechanical bounce after a short-horizon move is larger in geared names.
Profitability net of realized risk isolates quality that is not simply being paid for with volatility.
Cheap names that just sold off combine the value premium with short-horizon overreaction to flow.
Quality plus fresh attention: profitable firms need flow before the market re-rates them, and volume marks that flow arriving.
Cheap on book and low in its own recent range: two independent cheapness signals that both point to depressed sentiment.
Decay-weighted recent reversal applied where profitability caps the downside, so the most recent losses matter most.
A three-leg quality score: asset returns and pricing power minus gearing, which is the profitability that survives a credit squeeze.
Operating profit above reported ROA flags non-operating drags and one-off charges that later reverse out of earnings.
Profitable and cash-backed: accrual-heavy profits do not persist, so subtracting them isolates the durable part.
Real asset productivity net of accrual aggressiveness: revenue that turns assets is harder to fabricate than reported profit.
Debt plus aggressive accruals is the classic pre-writedown profile: obligations are hard while the earnings backing them are soft.
Reported EPS above what book and ROE imply flags one-off items that inflate the current print and reverse next quarter.
Operating quality on both DuPont legs, penalized for accrual aggressiveness that would make the quality illusory.
Book rising faster than retained earnings implies share issuance, and net issuance is a robust negative return predictor.
Profitability accelerating from one quarter to the next: acceleration leads the level and is not yet in consensus.
The direction of the fresh margin print, weighted by the level it lands at: good news matters more in an already-strong franchise.
When the report and the tape agree, confirmation extends the drift; disagreement usually means the print was already known.
A month-window profitability change keeps fresh reports with a short memory, decaying out stale quarters quickly.
High margins without lottery-like tails: extreme daily payoffs attract speculators who overpay and depress future returns.
Quality with a quiet recent tape: noisy quality is usually contested quality, with information still being discovered.
Profitability net of the width of the return distribution: the same profit is worth more when the tails are narrower.
The quality-plus-low-volatility pairing that leverage-constrained investors structurally underweight in favour of high-beta names.
Adding the two risk legs, gearing and realized volatility, targets the safe-asset side of both the credit and volatility anomalies.
Asset efficiency with a calm tape: operational quality that is not already the subject of an active repricing debate.
Return on equity per unit of short-run risk, the risk-adjusted quality that constrained investors cannot lever into.
Abnormal turnover in profitable names marks institutional accumulation, which pushes the re-rating of quality forward.
Quality net of Amihud price impact: pay for profits, not for the illiquidity premium that will not survive trading costs.
Efficient operators seeing volume expansion get repriced first, because operating news reaches the tape through trading.
Cheap at the lows on heavy trade is capitulation into value, where the marginal seller is done and supply is exhausted.
Recency-weighted volume expansion in high-ROE names dates the arrival of new holders more sharply than a flat average.
Quality plus a buy-on-strength volume pattern indicates accumulation by size buyers rather than passive drift.
Value with fading trading interest is the neglected-firm premium: low attention keeps the discount open until it closes abruptly.
Cheap relative to how profitable it is: the residual of value on quality is the part of the discount quality cannot explain.
Earnings power per dollar of price built from assets rather than reported EPS survives write-offs that distort the EPS line.
